- **D83 After a same-revision re-run, the switch-back returns to the pair an earlier app replaced (2026-11-10;
  refutation round 3, finding 14).** phase_switch_back took its target from the newest successful app receipt only.
  After any same-revision re-run, that receipt names this revision, so switch-back refused "there is nothing to switch
  back to" for good, while OLD's image was present and an earlier receipt named OLD. The re-runs are:
  - a provider-mode switch;
  - an access check run again;
  - the re-run a failed app's receipt asks for once its parked pair is removed.

  This was pre-existing (c2e53f8e gives the identical refusal). But D51 made switch-back the only post-success way back
  to c2e53f8e on live-shaped data: rollback-app's conservative read refuses on the 24 legacy encounters D51 measured.
  Now switch_back_target, when the newest successful receipt replaced this same revision, reads the target from the
  newest app receipt of this revision written since its last successful switch-back (to any target) that names another
  revision whose image is still present. A receipt whose image is gone is passed over. With none, there is still
  nothing to switch back to, and the message keeps its words. The since is read from that receipt: its own started_at
  plus D82's set.
  - Finding 14 (b) needs a receipt that is NOT ok. The first app over OLD installed its pair, its recompute failed, and
    its receipt's recovery was followed. Its receipt is the only one naming OLD.
    - So a not-ok receipt counts here when it records the web it replaced (replaced_web).
    - Only a switch that finished records one: S5's retire_live_web, or a swap's park, followed by a failed recompute,
      a failed removal of the parked pair, or a failed access check.
    - An undo, the S4 keep layout and an S5 failure record none, so after them there is still nothing to switch back
      to. INSTALL.md says that rollback-app is then the way back.

- **D85 A reconciliation note is never read as a retry release (2026-11-10; refutation round 3, finding 16; amends FINAL
  11.3, D52 and D60).** FINAL 11.3 writes the release on the run's reconciled_by, reconciled_at and
  reconciliation_note and queues 'interpret:...:retry:<run>'; that wording is superseded here. released_for_retry read
  reconciled_at plus reconciliation_note == RETRY_RELEASE_NOTE as a release. That
  column also holds an operator's free text, stored unchanged after strip() (operator.py), so a reconciliation note
  reading exactly 'released for one retry' counted as a release. No retry had run, and no 'interpretation.retry' audit
  row existed. Two probes showed the cost:
  - Probe A: the next upload of the same text sent again (1 send, provider 'succeeded').
  - Probe B: a member's retry, after the after-reconcile reading overran, sent again (1 send), where D60 promises 0.

  Now:
  - released_for_retry reads only the system-written 'retry-release:<run>' stage key, on any run carrying the answer.
  - retry_reading keys every release 'retry-release:<run>'. That includes a run nobody had reconciled, which until now
    was keyed 'retry:<run>' and released by the note.
  - On such a run it still writes who and when (RETRY_RELEASE_NOTE) as the record of the act. That record is never
    read.
  - A retry that releases nothing keeps 'retry:<run>' (D60). So does a second ask after a stopped release, where the
    release stands on the first stage's key; before, that ask was the first key plus ':resume:'.

  No other marker is needed: D52's path already releases by this key.
  - Measured on synthetic probes through the real operator and member doors, a4dcbea72 -> the repair:
    - Probe A: 1 send -> 0 (reused), with the note exactly as written and padded with spaces;
    - Probe B: 1 send -> 0 (reused).
    - D52's sequence and D60's measured paths are unchanged (their pins pass).
  - Cost:
    - A release a4dcbea72 wrote for a run nobody had reconciled (the note plus a 'retry:<run>' stage) is no longer a
      release. Such a stage, not yet run, stops at the failed-before door with nothing sent. The next retry releases
      the run under 'retry-release:<run>', keeps the note it finds, and sends once. This fails closed and is pinned.
      Production holds no interpretation run (c2e53f8e has no interpreter).
    - A release now exists only as a Job row, as D52's path already did. No code deletes Job rows, and their foreign
      keys are PROTECT. A release whose stage row were gone would read as no release: it fails closed.
  - Existing tests changed, because the release is now the key:
    - test_pipeline_interpret ReuseTests.test_p2_a_run_released_for_retry_is_never_reused: the release is set up as
      its 'retry-release' stage, not as a note.
    - FailedBeforeAndRetryTests.test_a_failed_reading_is_not_sent_again_until_a_recorded_retry_releases_it: the key
      is 'retry-release:<run>'.
    - FailedBeforeAndRetryTests.test_one_release_is_one_attempt_and_a_retry_that_fails_again_blocks_again: the
      second ask is 'retry:<run>'.
    - test_retry_reading_api MemberRetryTests.test_a_reviewer_retries_a_failed_reading_once_and_it_is_read: the key
      is 'retry-release:<run>', and the module docstring now says so.
  - Pins, in test_retry_reading_api OperatorNoteIsNoReleaseTests:
    - test_d85_probe_a_an_operators_note_reading_released_for_one_retry_leaves_the_stored_answer_reusable (both note
      forms);
    - test_d85_probe_b_a_members_retry_after_the_reading_overran_reads_the_stored_answer_again;
    - test_d85_only_the_system_written_retry_release_stage_is_a_release;
    - test_d85_the_release_of_a_run_nobody_reconciled_is_its_retry_release_stage;
    - test_d85_a_release_written_only_as_the_note_is_none_and_the_next_retry_releases_it: the cost.

    D52's and D60's pins pass unchanged: ReconciledRetryTests (2), and UnreadAnswerRetryTests in both modules (3 and
    2).
  - Mutations:
    - the note read again (mut-8): probe A (2 sends, provider 'succeeded', in both forms), probe B (2 sends), the
      stage pin and the cost pin fail;
    - an unreconciled release keyed 'retry:<run>' again (mut-9): the writer pin and the 3 changed retry tests fail;
    - jobs.py as at a4dcbea72 (mut-10): 9 fail.

    The D52 and D60 pins pass under all three.

- **D101 h3 reads every UNRESOLVED relation of the act (2026-11-11; the round-4 refutation of 437b708bb, finding 3;
  repair "questions").** events._h3_unresolved returned on the act's FIRST stored UNRESOLVED relation, so a same-event
  contradiction stored after another relation was never asked and its sentence appeared nowhere in the assessment.
  Finding 3's input: the sigmoid cold snare 45385 cites, "These were the findings at her index colonoscopy: no
  polypectomy was performed." (UNRESOLVED(time): its time words are the framing sentence, current_unanchored) and then
  C1CL3-001's "No polypectomy was performed in the prior segment." (UNRESOLVED(target, site_unresolved)). 437b708bb
  asked the snare's own, verified, time; with "Neither the EMR electrosurgical snare nor cautery was used to treat this
  polyp." (UNRESOLVED(technique), device_missing) first, its own verified technique. Listed the other way round, both
  asked statement_scope. Against C1CL3-001's expectation the framed-first order scored dropped_question; c2e53f8e asks
  conflict:snare in every order.
  - The rule. For a code, _h3_unresolved reads every UNRESOLVED relation of the act. A same-event contradiction
    (_h3_asks_contradiction: a denial's relation on the target or the scope, or D102's) is the code's question in any
    stored order: the first one resting on the TARGET (D86's own arm: where the pairing table rests on the target, every
    row before it - procedure, time, performer, technique - read the same), else the first one stored. With none, the
    first relation stored asks its attribute's fact, as before. The question's events and passages are the chosen
    relation's, so the prior-segment sentence is shown (question_events E2, E4). focus_question (FINAL 7.8, ``code``
    '') still reads the first relation only (D86's boundary).
  - Why the target first, which the spec does not state: D102 makes the framed denial's own time relation a
    contradiction too, so "the first contradiction stored" would ask about the framed denial and the prior-segment
    sentence would still be shown nowhere in the finding's own order. The spec's example ("the C1CL3-001 contradiction
    listed after an aside's time relation is asked") needs the target one. Mutant 2 below is "the first contradiction
    stored".

  only, so a denial whose OWN time, performer, device or session is the unknown side made the code ask the act's own
  VERIFIED attribute, with a reason that is not true. Finding 4's S2w: "During withdrawal, no polypectomy was performed
  in the sigmoid colon." ('During withdrawal' is no present-encounter frame, so the denial's time is unverified) beside
  the verified sigmoid snare: 45385 asked "Was the snare removal ... done at this encounter?" with "CPT Studio could not
  confirm from the document when the snare removal ... was done". Recorded: FRESH-2 A/note8 r3 45385 asked "Which
  technique was used for the snare removal (cold snare) ...?" beside its verified cold snare (the denial's hot snare
  unverified). S3 (two done examinations and "No polypectomy was performed.", session_unresolved) asked "In which
  procedure ...?". c2e53f8e asks conflict:snare on all three.

    (statement_scope) when the ACT's own value of that attribute is usable: the unknown side is then the statement's.
    When the act's own value is unusable, the relation keeps that attribute's question (D91, and D86 residual (b)'s
    direction: the act's own unanchored time, unknown performer or unverified device - pinned). A status, kind or part_of
    relation keeps performed_status (D91: C1CL2-002, C2CL-008, v4). The target and scope arms are D86's and D91's,
    unchanged.

- **D105 A stent removal and a stent placement in one duct are a possible stent exchange (2026-11-11; the round-4
  refutation, finding 22).** "The existing biliary stent was removed with a snare." and "A 10 Fr x 9 cm plastic biliary
  stent was placed into the common bile duct.", read to the contract as stent_removal and stent, made 43275 and 43274
  both READY, and 43276 on "Procedure: ERCP with biliary stent exchange." was held "not documented". A stent removed and
  replaced in the same duct at one session is one exchange (43276), not a removal and a placement. Nothing read the two
  acts together: coverage.bundled_reason (D45) folds only a sphincterotomy or a dilation into a stent act, and
  combination.competition compares E* sets, which do not intersect. The installed release never READYs 43275 there
  (its reader has no stent_removal kind) and READYs 43274.
  - The rule (studio/interpretation/ercp.py, exchange_pairs and exchange_hold). An ERCP session with a positive stent
    removal and a positive stent placement whose ducts nothing sets apart is a possible exchange. Each side is of the ERCP
    family, stated positive (verify.POSITIVE) and possibly current (D62), each read as a value in any verification state
    (D74's reading; D87: a doubt is a question), and not verified as another performer's act. Two ducts both verified and
    different (coverage.duct_side: the bile duct and the pancreatic duct) keep the acts separate. A duct verified on
    neither act, or the ampulla, never sets them apart (D45's reading).
    - A READY 43275 whose own stent removal is a side, and a READY 43274 whose own placement is a side, are held with ONE
      question naming the exchange (performed_status): "Were the stent removal (snare) at the bile duct (“was removed
      with a snare”) and the stent placement at the common bile duct (“was placed”) one stent exchange (43276), or
      separate services (a stent removal, 43275, and a stent placement, 43274)?". The question's events are the removal
      and the placement, and the decision reads both, so coverage counts both as read.
    - 43276, READY or held "not documented", is held with that question while the session has a pair. It is never "not
      documented" there.
    - A code held for another reason keeps its own question (D89; the removal's unanchored time keeps 43275's event_time
      question). An exclusion stands. Reason 'possible_exchange' (a new Evaluation.reason value; none is a closed list).
  - Where it runs: ercp.ruled is events.evaluate's ONE call site, its first statement. For a code D105 or D106 reads,
    it has the per-code rule evaluate the code once, re-entered with the hook stood down by a context variable, and
    applies the rules to that evaluation. For any other code it returns None and the rule goes on as before. So every
    reader of the per-code rule reads one evaluation: the assessment, its participants and second review, and
    overlay.counted_codes, which re-makes "the evaluation the engine made". A hook in assess alone would have made the
    review overlay's coverage differ from the engine's.
    - A decorator on evaluate was built first and refused. tests.test_guard_mutation's F3 plant recompiles
      events.evaluate from events.py's own source, and a wrapper defined in ercp.py is no FunctionDef there (3 errors).
      The in-function call site keeps evaluate the function events.py defines, and the plant applies and goes red, as
      before.
  - A literal choice, for the owner: 43276 READY on its own stent_exchange event beside such a pair (the refuter's
    three-event shape, where all three codes were READY) is held too ("43276, when proposed, is held with that
    question"). On a single exchange restated as three events that is a false hold of the right code. The other reading,
    hold 43276 only where it was "not documented", would leave 43276 READY beside two held rivals.
  - Pins: D105PossibleStentExchange, six tests:
    - finding 22's document with 43275+43274, +43276, and each code alone, with and without the participants (10
      subtests);
    - finding 22's second document ('Impression: Biliary stent exchange.'): 43275, 43274 and 43276 held, 43260 keeps

    - the three-event shape;
    - the controls: the ducts verified apart, either way round, keep 43275 and 43274 READY and 43276 not documented;
    - a duct not stated, and a placement at the ampulla, are a pair;
    - the removal's time unanchored: 43275 keeps event_time, 43274 and 43276 are held. A removal verified at an earlier
      encounter, or denied, is no side: 43274 READY.
  - Mutations: mut-2h (the rule off) fails 15 subtests over 5 tests. mut-5h (the call site removed) fails every D105

  25).** "The bile duct was swept several times with an extraction balloon; no stones or sludge were retrieved.", read
  as a performed stone_extraction (KINDS has no sweep; the extraction_balloon technique verifies on "extraction
  balloon"), made 43264 READY. CPT reports a removal of calculi or debris, and not a balloon passed through a duct
  that yields none. The installed release EXCLUDES 43264 (act_denied, its reader reads "no stones or sludge w..." as a
  negated stone_extraction), and holds it when Corti cites only the first clause.
  - The rule (ercp.nothing_retrieved, retrieval_hold). A supporting stone_extraction of 43264's one requirement group
    whose own sentence states that nothing was retrieved does not support 43264. "Its own sentence" is a sentence of its
    own located passages (kind, status, target) that holds one of its own words, or the whole of a passage none of
    whose sentences does (a restatement). "States" means: a negator (lexicon.NEGATORS, or n't) over STONE_WORDS (stone,
    stones, calculus, calculi, debris, sludge), at most three words between and no clause break, AND a retrieval or
    extraction word in the sentence (retrieve, extract, remove, deliver, recover and yield, with their forms).
    - With no other supporting act, 43264 is held with the performed_status question naming that sentence: "Was any
      stone, calculus, debris or sludge removed with the stone removal (extraction balloon) at the bile duct (“...; no
      stones or sludge were retrieved.”)?". Reason 'nothing_retrieved'. Never READY. The installed release's EXCLUSION
      is not ported: the hold is the fail-closed answer (D5; EB1 forbids an exclusion read from a passage's words).
    - With another supporting act (a basket extraction that did retrieve stones), 43264 stays READY on that act alone.
      The sweep leaves E* and stays in the decision's read events, so it is still covered.
  - An interpretation, stated: an exceptive or partial word between the negator and the stone word (further, other,
    additional, more, residual, remaining, retained, all, every, each, both, only) is not "nothing retrieved". ADJUDICATION
    C-7 reads "no further / no other / no additional" as about acts BEYOND those reported, never pairing with positive
    acts. So "Two stones were extracted ...; a final sweep retrieved no further stones." keeps 43264 READY, and so does
    "Not all stones could be extracted.". Pinned (test_d106_the_negation_read_in_the_acts_own_sentence), mutation-proved
    (mut-9h).

    attribute it verifies: the negation is in no attribute's words, since Gemini gave the act performed. EB1 says "a

    act's own sentence, never a neighbour. EB4 says a passage word list is never the repair.

- **D109 The same-day E/M rule reads an act by its kind, places an act "earlier in the day" on the date of service, and
  counts a non-GI or unidentified act only as an act of this encounter (2026-11-11; the round-4 refutation of
  437b708bb, findings 13, 23, 14, 15 and 16; amends D81 and D94; repair key em-same-day).** Three defects of
  combination.procedure_day and facts.day_of, each measured against c2e53f8e (studio.validation.engine.assess, driven
  as tests/test_harness_engine.py drives it) on byte-identical texts.
  - **By kind (findings 13 and 23).** An in-office band ligation, or an anoscopy, that Gemini files under the visit
    (procedure office_em: the prompt's "the heading or line that introduces the part of the document the act is in",
    and an office note's only heading is the visit's) had family gi.office_em. That family is outside
    SAME_DAY_FAMILIES, and the family test ran before any usability check. So the act made no procedure day, even when
    its procedure was unverified (procedure_unsettled), and 99213 was READY: "No same-day procedure is documented".
    c2e53f8e holds 99213 with separate_em: "Other GI service is documented as performed on the same date". The same
    held for em_other and sedation.
    - The rule. combination.SAME_DAY_KINDS is computed from the catalogue: every kind a procedural family's entry
      lists (acts, bundled and unsupported acts), the examination kinds and the umbrellas. That is every schema kind
      except em_visit, em_prolonged, moderate_sedation and other. An act of such a kind, filed under a family outside
      SAME_DAY_FAMILIES (gi.office_em, gi.em_other, gi.sedation), is a same-day procedure. Its label is OTHER_GI's,
      "Other GI service", the installed routing's reading. It counts as C-3 counts an event: its time is
      current_encounter in any state, or its own words place it on the date (facts.day_of ON). It is done only with its
      kind usable as well, since the kind is what makes it a procedure; otherwise it is possible. An examination whose
      device is verified manual (a digital rectal examination, E13) is not an endoscopic examination and never counts.
    - Reading of the spec. "A positive current event" is read as procedure_day reads every other event: a positive or
      uncertain status (D62 and D75: a doubt is never an absence), and "current" as C-3 defines a counted event. The
      undatable, non-current history mention filed under the visit is NOT counted, so an indication's banding asks
      nothing. That keeps finding 16's dead end (an event_time question whose only answers exclude the E/M) away from
      the kind arm. Recorded residual below (time 'unknown').
    - SAME_DAY_FAMILIES is unchanged, so D81's legacy pin stands.
  - **Same-date frames (finding 14).** facts.day_of read a verified earlier_encounter time worded "earlier in the
    day", "Earlier that day" or "Earlier in the morning" as OFF the date: an endoscopy at its own encounter earlier
    on the same date. 99213 was READY ("Stated but not as done today: upper endoscopy"); c2e53f8e holds it with
    separate_em. Pre-existing since S08 (SAME_DAY_WORDS).
    - The rule. lexicon.SAME_DAY_FRAMES (the spec's markers and their siblings: earlier or later today, in the day,
      that day, the same day, this or that morning, afternoon or evening, in the morning, afternoon or evening, on the
      same date, on the date of service) are read WHOLE, as D54 reads CURRENT_FRAMES. The time's own words, folded,
      edges stripped and split at commas, semicolons and a standalone "and", must be made of frames and nothing else.
      Then the act is ON the date whatever time Gemini gives. Never a bare "that day", "that morning" or "in the
      morning". facts._frame_parts writes D54's split without a pattern, and a pin holds it equal to
      lexicon._FRAME_EDGES and _FRAME_JOINS. SAME_DAY_WORDS is unchanged and still read anywhere in the words, so the
      frames only add.
  - **D94 narrowed (findings 15 and 16).** D94 counted every gi.unsupported act and every act of no family ('') by
    date of service.
    - fb13's attested shape (not_gi, current_encounter with no words, other_clinician "radiology service") for "CT
      images obtained today were interpreted separately by the radiology service." made 99213 ask separate_em.
    - fb14's attested shape (an abdominal ultrasound named in the indication, earlier_encounter worded "Indication:",

    - c2e53f8e is READY on both.
    - The rule. combination.CURRENT_ONLY_FAMILIES = {gi.unsupported, ''}. Such an act counts only when its time is
      current_encounter (any state) and its performer is not verified to another clinician or facility. D94's office
      excision and its unidentified act still ask separate_em (their pins pass unchanged).
  - **What the findings' inputs now give.** Each READY at 437b708bb becomes held with separate_em, as c2e53f8e holds

- **D110 Every app receipt of this revision after the bound counts toward the switch-back's since, whatever it
  replaced and however it ended (2026-11-11; refutation round 4, findings 21 and 20; amends D95 and D84).**
  replaced_since now counts every `app` receipt of this revision written after its last completed switch-back to the
  target (D82's bound). D95's served test is removed: a receipt that was successful, or one that parked a role
  (`_parked_anything`, 'replaced' non-empty). The bound, the target (D83), the order by stamp and D59's fallback are
  unchanged.
  - **Finding 21.** In an outage state, `app` is a swap: the HTTPS stage proxies to 9150 and no running web answers
    it.
    - The swap parks OLD's pair and starts this revision's web on 9150, in front of traffic. Its worker never becomes
      ready, so the undo restores OLD's pair.
    - The undo's close names e1 for a reason OLD's worker acts on, so OLD's worker is held. The receipt says "Install
      this revision again". It records hazards, stages_closed and states_put_back, and no 'replaced'.
    - D95 therefore dropped that window. A2 (blue/green over OLD, 10:30) gave the since. e1's record (10:03:30, in
      A1's window) was not touched, so the switch-back completed and B8 started OLD's worker while e1's hazard stood.
    - The installed release c2e53f8e refuses the same input. a4dcbea72 behaved as D95 does.
  - **Why not narrower.** A receipt cannot always say whether its phase put this revision's pair in front of traffic.
    - A swap's undo records only its close, and a swap that re-raises its first failure carries that failure's
      details.
    - "Could not then be closed / put back" carries none, and a KeyboardInterrupt writes a receipt with no details at
      all.
    - A refusal at the switch's start (switch problems, baseline drift) comes after migrate has run this revision's
      migrations.
    - The verifier's counterfactual (count a receipt that carries 'stages_closed') closes finding 21's exact shape and
      no other. mut-8 below measures it.
  - **Finding 20.** INSTALL.md (Switching back) and the replaced_since and phase_switch_back docstrings stated D82's
    rule, and the D84 pin enforced it. They now state the since as D95 and D110 read it:
    - every `app` receipt of this revision written after the last successful `switch-back` to that pair, whatever it
      replaced and however it ended (the kinds of receipt are listed);
    - an earlier time only refuses more;
    - a receipt whose order cannot be told is counted;
    - the pair's own status quo after that switch-back lasts until this revision's next `app` began;
    - a switch-back that did not complete, one to another revision and another revision's are no bound;
    - when the receipt the pair is read from is older than that switch-back, the time is that switch-back's own start.
  - **Measured.** All through the real install.main in BlueGreenWorld, using a probe in private copies of 437b708bb
    (D95) and of the work tree (D110). c2e53f8e was run through its own harness.

    | Input | D95 | D110 | c2e53f8e |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | Finding 21, swap undone, e1 'conflict', 'unknown' or 'outcome' | exit 0, since 10:30, OLD's worker started while e1 stands | exit 1, since 10:02:30, nothing started or stopped | exit 1 |
    | Finding 18, undone at S3 (nginx -t, and HTTPS after the reload), OLD's 'unknown' or 'outcome' at 10:20 | exit 1, 10:02:30 | exit 1, 10:02:30 (unchanged) | not run |
    | Finding 19, three revisions | exit 1, 10:02:30 | exit 1, 10:02:30 (unchanged) | not run |
    | No first app, OLD's 'unknown' at 10:20 | exit 0, 10:30 | exit 0, 10:30 | exit 1 |
    | A1 failed at S1 (replaced={}), then the same | exit 0, 10:30 | **exit 1, 10:02:30** | exit 1 |
    | A1 refused before S1 (baseline drift), then the same | exit 0, 10:30 | **exit 1, 10:02:30** | exit 1 |

    - The real host's receipts were read only; docker was never called and nothing was written. /home/claude/cpt-studio-install-20261023
      holds 13 app receipts, all ok, one per revision, and no switch-back. The target and the since are unchanged for
      13 of 13 revisions (12 targets, and 1 "names no previous web").
    - The change is monotone. The counted set only grows and every branch takes a minimum, so since(D110) <= since(D95)
      on every receipt set. The since is read only by the touched filter (the refusal) and by the receipt's
      touched_since, so D110 only adds refusals.
  - **Cost: false refusals, fail-closed.** Nothing is handed over.
    - After an app of this revision that failed or was refused before its pair served, the since reaches that app's
      start: an S1 failure; a refusal before S1 (switch problems, baseline drift, credential checks); an interrupted
      app.
    - So a record the target wrote while it served alone before this revision's next app refuses the switch-back while
      it stands: 'unknown' until it is reconciled, 'outcome' until a member's addendum (D82).
    - The baseline-drift refusal is routine, because app.quillmd.com's release changes on every deploy of that
      co-tenant. So this cost is likelier than finding 18's path.
    - c2e53f8e refuses every such input too, because it reads undo_hazards whole.
    - A completed rollback-app is no bound either: only a completed switch-back to the target is.
  - **Existing tests changed, where D110 moves them.**

    - The one code-keyed target hook, D29's DILATION_SITES, words its hold as a dilation (wording.another_site), and
      wording.SITE_WORDS would raise KeyError on a new class.

    - So within the spec's files there is no way to hold 43240 on that input, nor to list the act.

    dilation was performed on” apply ...'.

      words (or D103's fallback) together with its target's and its scope's own words (events._h3_place).
    - Each place is quoted once, in document order:

- **D115 A hemostatic clip or injection whose own words state no bleeding is a bleeding control in doubt (2026-11-11;
  the round-4 family parity audit, EGD gap D, critical; amends FINAL 7.7's clip rule as mapping.catalogue_kind reads it;
  repair key egd).** catalogue_kind read any clip or injection whose purpose 'hemostasis' is verified as a bleeding
  control. The purpose is verified when its words bind (normalize.py:602), so the adjective alone made a control of
  bleeding.
  - The gap's input (audit case D1): 'The gastroscope was advanced to the second portion of the duodenum.' / 'A 12 mm
    clean-based ulcer was seen in the gastric antrum.' / 'Two hemostatic clips were placed across the ulcer.' Gemini: E2
    clip, performed, technique 'hemostatic clips', target L1, purpose hemostasis worded 'hemostatic' (the attested note8
    and C2MEM purpose shape). 43255 cites the clip sentence.
    - 1caaf0609: 43255 READY on "bleeding control (clip) of the 12 mm clean-based ulcer".
    - c2e53f8e (harness configured, as production runs it): 43255 held [performed_status], "The documented upper
      endoscopy leaves the bleeding control in doubt (...). Was a bleeding control performed on the date of service?"
      (HEMOSTATIC_ADJECTIVE, refutation multi-3).
  - The rule (mapping.catalogue_kind's bleeding-control arm, mapping.hemostasis_in_doubt, mapping.bleeding_stated). A
    clip or an injection with a usable hemostasis purpose and a usable 'performed' status is a bleeding control only
    when one of its OWN words (kind, status, target, device, purpose) states bleeding or names the hemostasis as the act:
    - BLEEDING_STATED: bleeding (bleed, bled, rebleeding), oozing, hemorrhage, spurting, a visible vessel, an adherent
      clot, stigmata of recent bleeding or hemorrhage, and the noun hemostasis ("for hemostasis", "to achieve
      hemostasis"; the installed rule reads any bleeding-control word but the adjective as the act);
    - not counted when a negator stands anywhere before it in the same words (lexicon.NEGATORS, non, absent, absence,
      free, negative, a contraction in n't: "no active bleeding, oozing or visible vessel", "the non-bleeding ulcer",
      "without stigmata of recent bleeding");
    - not counted in words that hold a prevention, risk, hedge, condition or other-occasion word (NOT_BLEEDING_NOW: "to
      prevent delayed bleeding", "to ensure hemostasis", "if bleeding recurs", "a previously bleeding ulcer").
    - Otherwise its catalogue kind is mapping.POSSIBLE_BLEEDING_CONTROL: a bleeding control in DOUBT. No code profile
      covers it, so no code is matched by it. The bleeding-control codes (43255, 43227, 44366, 44378, 44391, 45334, 45382)
      are held [performed_status], never READY. The injection codes (43236, 43243) take no act that may be a control of
      bleeding: held, as at 1caaf0609.
    - A statement that is not a usable 'performed' (a denial, a plan, a doubt, an attempt, status words that do not bind)
      keeps the bleeding control, so its own rule holds or excludes as before. FRESH's "No hemostatic cautery, hemostatic
      clipping, injection for bleeding, or band ligation was performed" still denies a control of bleeding (55 such
      denials, 27 in FRESH-2 and 28 in FRESH-1, unchanged).

- **D124 An act documented only in another role's entry holds its code (2026-11-11; the round-4 family parity audit,
  colon-sig gap 0; owner directive 2026-11-06, item 2: other-provider acts stay distinct from completed current
  services; repair key colon).**
  - The gap (high). No rule on the new path read where an act is documented. On the contract's frame defaults
    (performer documenting_team, time current_encounter, no words) an act told only in a nursing note or under a
    pathology report heading is done, and supports its code. The audit's inputs, each a structured colonoscopy report
    ('Colonoscopy report (fictional)' / 'Place of service: ...' / 'Procedure: Colonoscopy' / 'The colonoscope was
    advanced to the cecum and the examination was completed.'):
    - T02: 'Nursing note' / 'Nurse: A 6 mm polyp in the sigmoid colon was removed with a cold snare and retrieved.',
      45385 citing the nurse's line.
    - U05: 'Nursing note' / 'Nurse: Cold forceps biopsies of the sigmoid colon polyp were obtained and sent to
      pathology.', 45380.
    - T03: 'Pathology report' / 'Sigmoid colon polyp, cold forceps biopsy: tubular adenoma.', 45380.
    - 1caaf0609: READY on all three, no question, coding complete_pending_review.
    - c2e53f8e (engine.assess as tests/test_harness_engine.py drives it, same texts and codes): held [performed_status].
      T02 and U05 with engine._another_roles_hold's question, "The snare removal is documented only in the nursing
      entry (“Nurse: ...”). Was it performed in this colonoscopy on the date of service?"; T03 act_missing ("CPT
      Studio could not find a forceps biopsy in the documented colonoscopy. ...").
  - The rule (events.another_role_hold, called once in evaluate, after the bundling holds and before the performed and
    incomplete returns). A code the per-code rule would support is held when EVERY act it accounts for (its supporting
    events but the examination, which is the session: C-1) is told only in another role's entry. An act is so told when
    every located place of its KIND and STATUS passages lies in one:
    - the passage begins with a role label, as a whole label: a name and its colon ('Nurse:', 'RN:', 'Pathology:',
      'Anesthesia:', 'CRNA:'), or an entry phrase followed by its end, a colon, a bracket or a dash ('Nursing note',
      'Nursing procedure record', 'Pathology report', 'Anesthesia record', 'Radiology report');
    - or, read from the document's lines: the line it stands on opens with such a label; or the line is a role's
      heading line (a heading name alone, 'NURSING', 'Pathology:'; or an entry phrase with at most a bracketed note, a
      date or time after a colon or dash, a closing colon); or it lies in the lines after such a heading line and
      before the next heading. The next heading is services.GENERIC_HEADING's shape (c2e53f8e): a line of at most 61
      characters opening with a capital or a digit, of letters, digits and / & , ( ) ' - only, at most a closing colon.
      A blank line does not end an entry. An act's own line is content, never the next heading.
    - never a line the physician's own label opens ('Endoscopist: ...', 'Physician addendum: ...').
    - Never a label or heading: 'Nursing staff: ...', 'Nurse: Jo Rowe, RN' and 'RN: Jo Rowe' as staff fields (they
      label their own line only and head nothing: services.ROLE_HEADINGS' refutation r1 missed-1), 'Nurse present
      throughout the procedure.', FRESH's own 'Anesthesia, equipment, and quality measures', 'Recovery instructions and
      management plan' and '- Pathology from jars 1-3 will be sent ...'.
    - An act with any statement passage outside such entries leaves the code as it is (U06: the physician's own line,
      alone or restated by the nurse; and a code over the physician's own biopsy beside the nurse's), and so does a
      code that accounts for no act (a base code, an examination-only EUS code: c2e53f8e's match lists no act either).
    - The hold: Evaluation reason 'another_role' (events.ANOTHER_ROLE, c2e53f8e's reason), state uncertain, E* empty
      and the acts in ``read``, so coverage still counts them as the code's (they are listed nowhere as uncovered, as
      the installed release's held match keeps its acts). ONE question, performed_status, worded as c2e53f8e words it -
      the entry's role and the act's first passage in it, quoted at 120 characters; the detail is "The colonoscopy is
      documented as performed with ... But the snare removal it accounts for is documented only in the nursing entry
      (...), not by the physician performing the colonoscopy. Held for the reviewer, not excluded." Never an exclusion.
  - Three readings beyond the spec's words, each only ADDING holds against its literal reading:
    1. The act's kind and status passages, not OWN's (kind, status AND target). The target's passages can be where the
       physician describes the LESION: 'Findings: A 6 mm sessile polyp in the sigmoid colon.' / 'Nursing note' /
       'Nurse: The polyp was removed with a cold snare and retrieved.' with the snare's target passage the findings
       line. Read as OWN, that place is outside the entry and 45385 is READY (mutant M5); c2e53f8e holds it with its
       another-role question. Kind and status are a subset of OWN, so the rule holds wherever the literal one does.
    2. "The passage begins with a role label" includes the line it stands on: Gemini may cite the clause after the
       label (prompt.py: "a sentence, a clause or a line"). 'A 6 mm polyp ... retrieved.' cited from 'Nurse: A 6 mm
       polyp ... retrieved.' with no heading above: READY without it (mutant M16); c2e53f8e holds it.
    3. The examination is not an act (C-1). A base code's supporting event is its session, and c2e53f8e lists no act

- **D139 A role's entry heading is read as the installed release reads it, and a code D124 holds lists its act
  (2026-11-11; the round-5b review of D124, round5b/review_colon.json problems 0-4, 9 and 10; repair key colon2).**
  - The gap (critical: problems 0-2). D124's heading_of read an entry phrase as a heading only when nothing, a closing
    colon, one bracket, or a date or time after a colon or a dash followed it, and it had neither the entry word
    'checklist' nor 'Procedure checklist'. c2e53f8e's services.ROLE_HEADINGS reads an entry phrase followed by at most
    60 characters of anything. heading_end then read such a heading as the NEXT heading, so the entry closed on its own
    heading line, and an act told only under it supported its code. The review's inputs, each the audit's structured
    colonoscopy report:
    - seven nursing headings - 'Nursing note - recovery', 'Nursing note, recovery room', 'Nursing note by Jo Rowe, RN',
      'Nursing note.', 'Nursing checklist', 'Procedure checklist', 'NURSING NOTE (Jo Rowe, RN) 08:30' - each in two
      shapes: the heading, 'Nurse: Patient tolerated the procedure well.', then the physician-worded snare line; or
      T02's snare clause directly under the heading. 45385.
    - five pathology headings over T03's biopsy line: 'Pathology report - final', 'Pathology Report: Final', 'Pathology
      report dated 11/12/2026', 'Pathology report, final diagnosis', 'Surgical pathology report - received
      11/12/2026'. 45380.
    - 46e461e7f: all 19 READY (supported), no question. c2e53f8e (engine.assess as tests/test_harness_engine.py drives
      it, on the same texts and codes): all 19 held [performed_status] - the 14 nursing inputs with its another-role
      question, word for word as this build now asks it; the 5 pathology inputs with act_missing ('CPT Studio could not
      find a forceps biopsy in the documented colonoscopy. ...'), as on T03 itself.
    - Problem 4 (low): _ROLE_HEADING_MARKS allowed ' and ’, which GENERIC_HEADING ([A-Za-z0-9 /&,()\-]) does not.
      'Nursing note' / "Patient's vital signs stable throughout" / the snare line: 46e461e7f READY (the line ended the
      entry); c2e53f8e held.
    - Problem 3 (medium, pins): no pin read 'RN:', 'Pathology:', 'Anesthesia:', 'Anesthesia record' or 'Radiology
      report'; the review's mutants MF, MG, MH and MI survived.
    - Problem 9 (low): a code D124 holds had support['acts'] == [] (assess._support listed acts only for conflict and
      bundled holds); c2e53f8e's another-role hold lists the act (T02, U05).
    - Problem 10 (low): jobs._assess_child_events' docstring said the revision text is read only for the exactness of
      the proposers' spans and the member answers' passages.
  - The rule:
    1. heading_of: an entry phrase that opens its line heads its role's entry when at most 60 characters follow it,
       whatever they are (_ROLE_HEADING_TAIL; ROLE_HEADINGS' [^\n]{0,60}$). It is read before D124's bracket, date and
       time reading, which stays, so no line D124 read as a heading stops being one, and no line changes role (no two
       roles' names or phrases open the same line).
    2. 'checklist' is a nursing entry word ('Nursing checklist', 'Nursing procedure checklist'), and 'Procedure
       checklist' is a nursing entry form with no role name (a seventh element in each _ROLE_FORMS row, read by
       entry_rest; ROLE_HEADINGS' procedure\s+checklist).
    3. heading_end never reads the entry's own heading line as the next heading. role_of asks heading_of first, and
       heading_of now reads every line that opens with an entry phrase and has at most 60 characters after it. A longer
       line has at least 68 characters (the shortest phrase is 'rn note'), and heading_end's bound is 61. So no separate
       guard was built: it could not change an outcome, and no mutant could kill it. The 19 pins fail if heading_end
       reads those lines (M1).
    4. _ROLE_HEADING_MARKS is " /&,()-": no apostrophe, as GENERIC_HEADING.
    5. assess._support: a code held ANOTHER_ROLE with no supporting event lists its question's events (the held acts)
       as support['acts'], beside the conflict and bundled arms. T02: [{'id': 'E2', 'kind': 'snare', 'label': 'snare
       removal (cold snare) of the 6 mm polyp in the sigmoid colon', 'status': 'performed'}]; c2e53f8e lists one act,
       kind 'snare', the same label. U05: kind 'biopsy', 'forceps biopsy (cold forceps) of the sigmoid colon polyp';
       c2e53f8e, kind 'biopsy', 'forceps biopsy at the sigmoid colon' (its reader's words). On the new path this changes
       the record and nothing it decides. The assessment's services record is the stub ('services': []), so
       questions.acts_of is empty: no question's passages or fingerprint move (the engine passes {} itself). The
       proposal fingerprint does not read support (T02 and U05: unchanged). The overlay reads act kinds only for
       supporting events.

  - The rules (studio/interpretation/ercp.py).
    - (1) _states_yield. A clause states a yield when a past yield verb (YIELD_VERBS) that no negator precedes has a
      stone word as its subject, and the clause holds no guard word.
      - The subject is the word before the verb, past at most two auxiliaries (was, were, has, have, been), and must be
        one of YIELD_SUBJECTS: stone, stones, sludge, debris, calculus, calculi, fragments.
      - The guard words: a purpose word ('to'; 'so that'; 'in order to' ends in 'to'), a condition or doubt word
        (whether, if, unclear, possible, possibly, may, might, suspected, any) or an other-time word (prior, previous,
        previously, earlier, index, last).
    - (1) The yield that clears D106's hold is read in two ways, each with _states_yield:
      - the structural reading (_own_yield, EB1): the act's own attribute words (kind, status, target and technique),
        each clause of those words read in those words alone, and only words that overlap no other event's own words
        (for example, 'Multiple stones were extracted' as the kind words);
      - the clause reading (_yields): a clause of the act's own sentence that holds one of its kind, status or target
        words and no other event's words. It is kept because the structural reading alone loses every clearance D127
        pinned, and c2e53f8e READYs each of them. None of those clearances has its yield in the act's attribute words:
        their kind words are 'extracted' and their status words 'were removed' or 'were extracted'.
    - (1) D127's 'to'/'be' guard is now covered by the subject rule: 'to' is a purpose word, and neither 'to' nor 'be'
      is a stone word or an auxiliary. _negated was read only by D127's _yields and is removed.
    - (2) The next-sentence read in nothing_retrieved never drops a following sentence that holds the words (kind,
      status or target) of an event whose status value is anything but 'performed' (PERFORMED), in any verification
      state. That covers a denial (not_performed), an uncertain statement, a plan, and an act begun and not completed. A
      following sentence that holds only performed events' words is still dropped (D127's problem 2: another act's
      sentence).
    - (3) assess._incomplete_session's docstring now says that D107's warn quotes the sentence that states the failure
      (D127), and quotes the failure-marker words alone only where no own sentence holds them.

    PER_SOURCE = 2), MAX_PASSAGES = 4 in all. D126 (0) put every contradiction's relation passages in the source, in

    the row.
    - Input A: finding 3's framed and device denials beside C1CL3-001's prior-segment denial, each on its own line,
      45385 citing the snare. 46e461e7f's row, in every one of the six sentence orders: [the snare, the first two
      statements]; the prior-segment sentence absent. Now: [the snare, the two same-site denials, the prior-segment
      denial]. Installed c2e53f8e (studio.validation.engine.assess as tests/test_harness_engine.py drives it, bare and
      with 'Procedure: Colonoscopy'): conflict:snare, its row the snare and all three statements.

      prior-segment denial, either order. 46e461e7f: [the snare, S2w line 1, S2w line 2]. Now: [the snare, S2w line 1,
      S2w line 2, the prior-segment denial]. Installed: conflict:snare (bare: plus extent), its row the snare, S2w as
      one span and the prior-segment denial.
    - Why validation/questions.py. No change inside events.py can show Input A's three statements: the row takes at
      most two passages from the source whatever events.py puts there, and the code's own cited passage (the snare)
      fills the other group. So, as the spec allows, fields only the new path sets. events._h3_shown, for a question
      about SEVERAL statements only, keeps the source exactly as before (every relation's passages, in the question's
      order, each once) and names on each place of a statement's own passages (its status, kind, scope and target
      passages: relations._passages' statement side) that statement's id (questions.STATEMENT = 'statement'), and marks
      as LEAD (questions.LEAD = 'lead') the place the question quotes the statement by - its status place
      (events._h3_quoted, the places _h3_whole_statement joins, the status place first) - and the act's place holding
      its status words, else its kind words. questions.question_passages reads them for the statement_scope fact only
      (questions.STATEMENT_FACT; passages takes ``named``, default False), through questions._statements_kept: after
      the matched and cited groups (as before), ONE passage of each statement - its lead, else its first - in the
      source's order, then the act's lead (else its first), then every other passage in the source's order, to
      MAX_PASSAGES; the chosen ones shown in the source's order, so a statement's lines stay together. _kept's loop is
      now _chosen with an optional cap per group; _kept returns exactly what it returned.

  - The rule (events.another_role_hold, its nested helpers and its tables only):
    1. _ROLE_NURSE covers services._NURSE in full, generated longest first: each lead ('', pre-procedure,
       preprocedure, intra-procedure, intraprocedure, post-procedure, postprocedure, recovery) with each name
       (nursing, nurse's, nurses, nurse, rn), plus 'lpn'. That is 41 names, a superset of e5628be56's 13. They are
       still the nursing row's names, heading names and entry names.
    2. role_of trims the act's line and each line above of ASCII whitespace only (_ROLE_SPACE: space, tab, CR, FF,
       VT). So a line a no-break or other Unicode space opens or ends is no next heading (heading_end). CRLF lines,
       tabs and trailing spaces still trim. The act's own line only feeds physician, label_of and heading_of, and each
       of these folds it (Python's split drops every character str.strip drops). So the act's line trim cannot change
       an outcome (M2a below is equivalent); the change that matters is the one to the lines above.
    3. label_of reads the line as fold reads it, and then from its first ASCII letter, digit or '_' (unlead). So a
       label may follow any characters that are not these, as ROLE_LABEL's ^\W* (re.A) reads it.
    4. signed is read where nothing else places the act in another role's entry: no label, no heading, no entry
       above. It takes the label the act's own line opens with: the text up to the last colon before the act's own
       words (the earliest of its kind's and status's words in the place). It reads that label for c2e53f8e's
       ROLE_SIGNATURE, re-typed as _ROLE_SIGNATURE:
       - nursing: a record word (recorded, entered, documented, completed, charted); 'by' and its space within 60
         characters after it; then RN, LPN or nurse within 60 characters. Or 'nursing', its space, and checklist,
         entry, note or handoff.
       - anesthesia: CRNA, anesthesiologist or anaesthetist, with recorded, documented or charted within 40
         characters after it.
       - Words stand whole (\b), no reach crosses a period, and letters fold over ASCII only (re.A | re.I).
       - It is read on a line the physician's label opens too, where it is the only reading (see reading 5).
       - A reading without the text (the overlay's counted codes, a unit test's Reading) reads the passage's own
         label the same way.
       - A signature anywhere else names no role.
    5. jobs._assess_child_events' docstring now says: the entry lines hold the act's code and never exclude one; a
       code so held supports nothing, so a rival that competed with it for the same act loses that competing_codes
       hold (the ERCP input, as c2e53f8e READYs both). The tables' comment now says phrase_end is \b but for '_'
       ('Nursing note_x' heads an entry here and not there: a cost already recorded in D139).

  - The rules (studio/interpretation/ercp.py).
    - (1) _yield_pairs is D140's subject rule, now giving each (subject, verb) it reads; _states_yield is the guard plus
      _yield_pairs, as before. 'fragments' (FRAGMENT_WORDS) is a subject only directly after one of YIELD_SUBJECTS
      (stone, stones, sludge, debris, calculus, calculi), and YIELD_SUBJECTS no longer holds it.
    - (2a) The clause reading (_yields): a clause of the act's own sentence that holds one of the act's own words (kind,
      status, target) and no other event's, and no guard word anywhere in the clause (_guarded over the whole clause, as
      before), states the act's yield only where a yield's verb and its subject stand in one SIMPLE clause that holds
      one of the act's own words (_simple_yield). A simple clause is the clause cut before each word of CLAUSE_OPENERS
      (after, before, since, when, whenever, while, once, until, till, as, because, although, though, whereas, where,
      and, but, then; _simple_clause), the words with their document offsets from _words (the folded words _tokens
      reads). The negator test stays over the clause before the verb, as D140 read it, so the cut never takes a yield
      D140 refused. states_nothing_retrieved (every simple clause the act's) changes only by (1). _denial's clauses are
      not cut.
    - (2b) The structural reading (_own_yield): the act's attribute words state its yield only where no clause of a
      located passage that holds those words carries a guard word - every located passage of the reading is read, so a
      guard word that any passage's clause holds around those words counts - and, as before, only in a clause of those
      words that holds no other event's words and no guard word. Words no located passage holds state none. The yield's
      verb and subject stand in one simple clause of those words (_simple_yield with no act's words to hold).
    - (3) nothing_retrieved's following-sentence filter: the sentence that follows an own sentence is dropped as another
      act's when it holds the own words (kind, status, target) of another event whose status value is 'performed', in
      any verification state (as D140 reads the value), and read when the only other events whose words it holds have
      any other value. D140's `unperformed` list is replaced by `performed`.

      reading, D147's following sentence), and a D147 paragraph follows D140's; nothing_retrieved's D140 item names
      _own_yield (the structural reading) and _yields (the clause reading); _yields' docstring states the simple-clause

  - What the held-back rules do (patch-heldback.diff: events.another_role_hold's nested signed, words_at and role_of
    only):
    1. signed(source, at, begin) reads the label from the start of the line on which the act's passage begins (`begin`),
       up to its last colon before the act's own words (`at`). That is no longer only the line the act's words begin
       on. It applies on both role_of arms that call it (the physician's line, and 'no entry places it'), and on the
       passage alone when the reading has no text (from the passage's own first line).
       - ROLE_SIGNATURE's [^.\n] reaches cross no period and no line break. These are a record word within 60
         characters before 'by', a nurse word within 60 after 'by' and its space, and an anesthetist word within 40
         before a record word.
       - The space after 'by' or 'nursing' (\s+ under re.A) may hold a line break.
    2. words_at reads each kind's or status's words after the last colon inside them. Words that open at a label thus
       leave the label before that colon to signed.

  - **The rule (events.another_role_hold's nested signed, words_at and role_of only).**
    1. D152 (1), exactly as round5e/colon4/patch-heldback.diff builds it (its events.py hunk, applied to f9013e12e
       without offset; another_role_hold is then AST-identical to colon4's held-back build).
       - signed(source, at, begin) reads the label from the start of the line on which the act's passage begins,
         up to its last colon before the act's own words. It does so on both role_of arms that call it, and on the
         passage alone when the reading has no text.
       - ROLE_SIGNATURE's [^.\n] reaches cross no period and no line break. The space after 'by' or 'nursing'
         (\s+ under re.A) may hold one.
    2. D152 (2), as built there. words_at reads each of the kind's and status's words after the last colon inside
       them, so words that open at a label leave that label to signed.
    3. D158's own reading, for colon4's K6. signed reads the label on the line of `at` (the act's own words) first,
       as f9013e12e reads it, and that role is the role. Only where that line names none is the label read from the
       passage's first line (rule 1).
       - Rule 1 alone read 'CRNA charted the sedation:' / 'Documented by Jo Rowe, RN: <snare>' as one label holding
         both signatures, and so named the anesthesia entry. f9013e12e and c2e53f8e both name nursing.
       - It decides no hold, and this holds by construction. With the same `at`, the label on the act's line is a
         suffix of the label read from the passage's first line. The two end at the same colon, the line break
         before the act's line is no word character, and no match inside one line crosses a line break. So a
         signature that names a role on the act's line names one in the longer label too.
       - So where f9013e12e's signed names a role, D158 names the same role, unless rule 2 moves `at` (see K6g
         below). Where it names none, D158 reads as rule 1 does.

    - _same_day_frame takes ``anywhere``. With it, the words are also ON when a lexicon.SAME_DAY_FRAMES entry stands
      whole anywhere in them, whatever other words they hold: the words folded (lexicon.fold), the frame's own folded
      words found contiguous, with no letter or digit touching either end. "earlier in the day, before her visit",
      "Before her visit, earlier in the day" and "I performed a flexible sigmoidoscopy earlier in the morning in the
      endoscopy suite" hold one; "earlier in the daytime", "earlier in the days before her visit", a bare "that day" and
      "in the morning" do not. An anaphoric frame (lexicon.ANAPHORIC_FRAMES) is never read that way. Without
      ``anywhere`` D109's whole reading is unchanged.
    - day_of reads it for an act whose own usable earlier_encounter or future time would place it OFF, whose performer
      is not verified to another clinician or facility (D132's condition, the same ``other`` reading) and whose words

  - The rule (assess._claims; no other function changes).
    - A code HELD by any hold - its evaluation's state 'uncertain' with no supporting event - keeps as claims the
      events its evaluation names (Evaluation.question.events) or read (Evaluation.read: the acts the hold was decided
      on), kept only where the code could account for the act, as it would claim it as supporting were its doubt
      resolved:
      - an act of its family and of a kind of its requirement groups (events.is_candidate over events.requirements);
      - stated positive or uncertain, possibly current (coverage.possibly_current, D62), and not verified as another
        performer's (D87: a doubted act is a doubt, an absent one is not);
      - for a code that names a technique, of its device class or not verified as a class, and not verified outside its
        D29 site class: _technique_doubts' reading. R4: a dilation of another technique is no act the code accounts
        for, as c2e53f8e's technique_fits reads it.
    - These claims are ADDED to what D55, D74 and D118 claim. Those still read the code's supporting events only and
      are unchanged, so the change only ever adds a competition pair. It never makes a code READY or excluded and never
      removes a question: the only readers of the claims are combination.competition and, through support['competes'],
      the member-answer reader and the read-time overlay, which release a competing hold only when its rivals are gone.
      E* (support.acts) is unchanged.
    - Structural only: no word list, no 're', no legacy reader (EB1: the decision reads the evaluation's own events).

  - **The rule (events.another_role_hold's nested helpers).**
    1. The label is read for the act's SENTENCE.
       - sentence_end gives the last sentence end in a span. It uses the engine's own boundary: '.', '!' or '?'
         (ercp.SENTENCE_ENDS) followed by whitespace or by the end of the text, as ercp._sentences ends a sentence. No
         word list.
       - A place begins mid-sentence when the text from the previous sentence end to its start holds more than
         whitespace. Its sentence begins at the first character after that end.
       - signed then reads from the start of that line as it reads from the passage's first line (D152), with the
         act's own line first (D158). This only grows the label, so it never loses a role the passage's own lines name.
       - words_later covers a place that holds none of the act's words. Its role is read up to the act's own words when
         those begin after it with no sentence end between the place's last character and them. It runs only after the
         old reading (the label closed before the place) found nothing, so it can only add a role. It is what holds the
         r5 form whose first line passage carries the label and none of the act's words.
       - With no text, a place's sentence cannot be read. For item (1) the no-text path is unchanged.
    2. The physician's own label, where the act's own line names no role. Two conditions must both hold:
       - the line opens with events.physician's label;
       - it opens in a form at which the installed release's _sentences starts a sentence, whatever ends the line above
         (opens_a_field). That is a list item ('-', '*' or '•' and a space), or a 'Label: value' field within the 39
         characters _sentences reads there: an ASCII capital, 1 to 40 ASCII letters, spaces or '/&()-', a colon,
         spaces or tabs, then a character that is no space.
       - Then no line above is read, and the act's role is the physician's.
       - A signature label closed before the act's words on that line is still read first. So D146's 'Endoscopist: see
         below. Documented by Jo Rowe, RN: <the act>' stays held.
       - It applies on both paths. The no-text path therefore returns to e5628be56's and f9013e12e's 'supported'.
       - Why the second condition (the spec, built as written, released holds c2e53f8e keeps; this narrows it). Take
         the line 'Documented by Jo Rowe, RN: patient positioned left lateral', with no sentence end. Under it, or under
         a line ending 'patient seen by Dr.', put any of these as the act's line:
         - 'endoscopist: <the snare sentence>' (lower case);
         - '> Endoscopist: ...', '# Endoscopist: ...' or '· Endoscopist: ...';
         - 'Endoscopist:<the snare sentence>' (no space after the colon).
         c2e53f8e runs the line above on into each of them, and its signature label closes before its act mention. It
         holds all of them in both configurations; so does 05a881a75. The condition of events.physician alone made them
         READY: 12 constructed inputs, released where c2e53f8e holds (probe/phys2). opens_a_field excludes them. Under a
         line that ends with a period they are READY on c2e53f8e but stay held here: costs, unchanged from 05a881a75.
    3. The lines above the act's own line are read one at a time, nearest first. The first whose label names a role
       names it.
       - Only where no single line does is the whole label read, as D152 reads it. That covers a signature whose \s+
         after 'by' or 'nursing' spans a line break, and one on a line with no colon of its own.
       - It changes the entry named, never whether one is named: a role that one line's label names, the whole label
         names too.
    - An exact short cut, for cost (see "Time").
      - Every signature holds a record word, an anesthetist word or 'nursing'. A span above the act's own line that
        holds none of them names no role, so it is skipped.
      - str.lower folds every ASCII letter that read folds, so the test never misses.
      - Checked when it was added (before item (2)'s field condition): 289 probe entries and 38 pin inputs gave
        byte-identical outcomes with and without it.

      own boundary, so it is not built. Examples: a lowercase continuation only; or treating a line that ends with a
      colon, a heading or a blank line as the end of the sentence.

    - _off_the_date calls day_of(event, None). That is the effective date's answer for every time that has an
      exclusion basis:
      - such a time is a usable earlier or future time;
      - its date literals all compare unequal to the date it was judged against (otherwise verify.time_words gives
        date_mismatch, and the time is unusable);
      - assess judges every time against the effective date (verify.rejudged);
      - day_of reads no frame beside a literal.
    - So the E/M's day (combination.procedure_day) gives the same answer.
    - facts is imported inside the helper, because facts imports nothing of events.

## Integration owner's decisions for design v2 (2026-11-12, session 68197eb1, continuing 30a58364)

- **D178 Design v2 is adopted after its refutation (FINAL-V2 8.1, step 0a).**
  - The design is `docs/gemini-migration/FINAL-V2.md` (sha256
    `9d650797c41091d3ab9ce2f783c1838e5aa394bb926c5d5b2733c2186d733b21`), committed with this entry and byte-identical to the
    session's `design-v2/FINAL-V2.md`. The judge's decision on each refutation finding is `docs/gemini-migration/REFUTATIONS-V2.md`
    (sha256 `59e39a0515c0a47055cba90735a3488be7b680114d2a809dde15d6c32dc7e5ad`). The text before the refutation stays in the
    session directory as `design-v2/FINAL-V2-pre-refutation.md` (sha256
    `cc5c288872a1c1a65af241997f12414a3e538b7e49eb6c2d043d3a6c5a796a00`).
  - How it was made (workflow wf_ea6e3b86-a83, 13 agents):
    - four surveys: contract, readers, rules, failures;
    - three competing designs: A extend, B requirements, C two-pass;
    - a judge's synthesis: C's two passes, B's requirement table, A's section inheritance;
    - four refutation lenses: self-certification, holds, contract, migration and operations;
    - 28 findings: 1 critical, 8 high, 15 medium and 4 low. 22 were accepted and 6 accepted in part; none was rejected whole;
    - the revision was applied by 157 replacements, each asserted to apply exactly once.

    Every agent was blind to acceptance-a1 and to every sealed set.
  - What the integration owner checked before adopting:
    - the directive's five required items against section 0's table, and each item against the sections it names;
    - every deterministic check of 3.1 can only make a fact UNRESOLVED. None sets, changes or removes a value, and none creates
      support, an exclusion, a contradiction or a READY;
    - what still touches document text (5.6), and nothing else does:
      - segmentation by character classes;
      - quote location;
      - L1's check of a date Gemini gave against its own words: it only demotes, and it is pinned to v1's eight parsers and their
        two tables;
      - revision binding;
      - R1's evidence integrity;
      - the participants' locator;
      - display.

      No vocabulary decides, confirms or vetoes a meaning;
    - Corti, Astra and Fable, reviewer approval and customer-facing confidentiality are unchanged (4.12), and no model agreement
      approves a code (3.5, 3.6);
    - 0a's gate: the a1 v2 hash commit `4b52bad86a539e55c66b3e1bab275d686d76bdff` (2026-11-12T04:41:17Z) exists and is on
      origin. No prompt byte and no send precedes the frozen acceptance set.
  - Conditions the integration owner adds:
    1. **The acceptance run follows THRESHOLDS.md, not 7.6's "x 3 runs".** 7.6 was written blind to the set's composition.
       - Three runs each: the 48 independent cases and g1's 12 documents.
       - One run each: the other 167 cases.
       - That is 347 documents: about $41 at November prices and about $82 from 2026-12-01, at the design's mean. A' is the
         same.
    2. **Overlap between development and acceptance is measured, not assumed away.**
       - The exclusion list catches only exact copies, yet a1's regression cases were rebuilt from the same failure evidence the
         development set holds.
       - Step 7 adds a near-copy report: each development document's highest character-shingle similarity to any a1 document,
         printed as ids and scores only.
       - No development document is withdrawn for it. A regression case is a known failure the build is meant to fix. Whether a
         fix generalises is measured by the paraphrase, variant and independent kinds.
       - The report gives each kind's result beside the overlap.
    3. **Owner items, each raised before the step it gates** (standing authority):
       - class d, before the install: the per-document cost of the second call (7.1), stated to the owner on 2026-11-12;
       - class d, before A: the recording budget against the cap and the month's recorded spend (7.6);
       - class b, before the install: a legacy approval does not carry across engines, and a context change on a legacy encounter

       - class d, before any batch after the switch: a separate test key or project (7.6);
       - carried from v1 and re-judged before the install: D37's EGD heading trade, and the re-check offer on two legacy

- **D179 ADJUDICATION on the v2 path (FINAL-V2 3.5).**
  - EB1 is kept and narrowed: deterministic checks read offsets, unit boundaries and Gemini's own date words only.
  - EB2 is retired: there are no frame defaults. Inheritance from a section replaces them; Gemini states it, geometry checks it
    and the second call appraises it.
  - EB3 is retired: there is no marker basis of exclusion. An exclusion needs an established explicit negative.
  - EB4 is kept: a residual is measured, and a false READY is repaired in the prompt, the schema, the claim templates or a coding
    rule, never with a word list.
  - ADJUDICATION.md itself is unchanged and still governs v1's records. On the v2 path these four amendments apply.

- **D180 Parity shims dropped and parity choices kept (FINAL-V2 4.13).**
  - Dropped, because each was a word reader or a word-derived stand-in (the fact that replaces it in brackets):
    - C-11's dismissal of Gemini's contradictions by "hard" literal rows, with the literal hardness of `time_row`,
      `procedure_row` and `performer_row`;
    - D58/D77's place adjacency read as causality (`part_of` and `cause`);
    - D127's cannulation "conflict" for a failure followed by success (`access_outcome`);
    - D115, D142, D149 and D157's bleeding words and adjective keys (`purpose` and `cause`);
    - D31's hold of a whole session on an open question. Each doubt now holds only the facts it names, and K2 touches only the
      act's own session fact;
    - the region moves of D114, D141, D148 and D153 (the act's own session fact);
    - the label and signature grammar of D124-D172 (the section owner);
    - the frames and markers of D35, D42, D54, D64 and D109-D162 (the date relation).
  - Kept, as rules over facts:
    - D157's doubt: a clip or injection whose purpose or cause is not established may be a bleeding control, so its denial never
      excludes;
    - D163 and D167: a held code keeps its claims;
    - D134: an office visit is set apart beside a done procedure session (a listing rule);
    - C-3 counts any performer's same-day procedure;
    - an act on the date of service at a separate encounter supports its code (T2).

    The last two are diagnostic against c2e53f8e (owner amendment of 2026-11-09: parity is diagnostic). They change only by a
    recorded coding rule, never by a reader.

- **D181 Five new question facts (FINAL-V2 4.8).**
  - Each fact joins `wording.NEW_FACTS` with its MISSING sentence, by the path v1 already uses for its seven new facts:
    - `event_entry`: "whose entry the act is told in";
    - `exam_stations`: "which parts of the upper tract were examined";
    - `act_yield`: "what the extraction retrieved";
    - `act_cause`: "what caused the bleeding the act treated";
    - `act_part`: "whether the act was part of another act".
  - A customer sees only the fixed sentence. Causes stay operator data (MO-2).

- **D182 One item per held code, by a fixed rank (FINAL-V2 4.8).**
  - Each held code carries exactly one clarification: the item of its highest-ranked unmet requirement on its chosen binding. It
    is a question when the fact is unresolved, and an explanation when an established fact fails the requirement.
  - RANK is pinned in `engine/requirements.py`, with 23 ranks. The first four keep v1's h1-h4 order:
    1. a contradiction;
    2. a doubt on status;
    3. a statement's scope;
    4. a status not established.
  - The binding, in order:
    1. kept-span overlap;
    2. the candidate whose top item ranks highest;
    3. the fewest unmet requirements;
    4. at an equal rank, a question before an explanation;
    5. document order.
  - Every candidate's unmet facts are kept in `support.held_facts`:
    - the operator sees them with their causes;
    - the reviewer sees them only as fixed sentences;
    - they are never asked as separate questions;
    - they are re-evaluated after an answer or an addendum.
  - Member answers are unchanged. The only answers are "Not documented" and "Cannot confirm", and an answer never confirms a fact
    or releases a hold.

- **D183 The owner's funding authority applied to design v2 (2026-11-12; supersedes FINAL-V2 7.6's three budget rules and
  part of D178 condition 3).**
  - The authority is verbatim in the rulings file ("Owner directive, 2026-11-12 — funding authority for the migration; the
    second Gemini call approved") and in RULINGS.md.
  - **The second call is approved.** The two passes stand, and 7.1's per-document cost is accepted.
  - **7.6 rule 1 is superseded.** The owner no longer receives a total before the acceptance run. The run's actual usage and
    cost are reported with its result.
  - **7.6 rule 2 is superseded.** There is no project-level stop, and no total or monthly ceiling of the session's own.
    - Each batch keeps a cost guard of about twice its modelled cost at the prices of the day. The guard stops a runaway
      loop; it is not a ceiling on the work.
    - A batch that reaches its guard stops. Its measured cost resizes the next batch, and no approval is sought.
  - **7.6 rule 3 is closed.** No separate key or project is created; keys are the owner's, and this authority creates none.
    - After the switch, test batches share the Google project with the installed site.
    - A provider cap or quota 429 is an installation-wide hold that pauses new uploads. It is diagnosed at once and reported
      to the owner, never retried in a loop.
    - Post-switch test batches stay small, and the site's usage stays visible in the operator report.
  - **D178 condition 3, item by item:**
    - the second call: approved;
    - the budget before A: superseded;
    - the post-switch key: closed, since none is created;
    - the class-b legacy context-save loss: STILL OPEN, and asked again before the install.
  - **The ledger.** `gemini-migration/USAGE-LEDGER.md` continues from the recorded history; nothing is credited or reset.
    - Each batch appends its actual usage (provider-reported tokens) and its cost.
    - Estimated costs are labelled as estimates, and unknown costs stay unknown.
    - Consumed attempts and failures stay listed.
  - Unchanged: D178 condition 1 (the acceptance run follows THRESHOLDS.md) and condition 2 (the near-copy report).

- **D184 Automatic recheck after a save; the mandatory "Check again" is removed (owner amendment, 2026-11-12; supersedes
  FINAL-V2 6.2's manual re-check, MO-4's resolution, and closes D178's class-b item).**
  - The owner's words are verbatim in the rulings file ("Owner amendment, 2026-11-12 — automatic recheck after a save")
    and in RULINGS.md.
  - **Superseded:** FINAL-V2 6.2 "Legacy encounters and context saves" (store the values, queue nothing, explicit
    "Check again"), the matching sentence in 7.4, and that part of 8.1 step 5b.
  - **Closed:** D178 condition 3's class-b item. The owner chose automatic rechecking over the loss.
  - **The rule,** for legacy and new encounters alike:
    - a successful save that changes clinical content or coding context queues the recheck in the background;
    - only the stages whose inputs changed run;
    - each result is bound to the exact revision and context;
    - an older result never displaces newer work;
    - duplicates are prevented;
    - while it is pending, the earlier codes cannot be approved or exported as current;
    - when it completes, the updated codes and what changed are shown, and approval stays explicit;
    - failures offer Retry, and quota, authentication and payment failures hold without repeated requests.
  - **No provider call** on typing, on a save with no changed value, or on a change no coding rule reads.
  - **On a v2 revision with an inventory,** a context save sends nothing to Gemini.
  - **On a legacy revision,** the two passes run once per revision and are reused by request hash.
  - **The precise behaviour** (triggers, coalescing of rapid successive saves, the current-assessment compare-and-set,
    progress, the what-changed view, the stale guards on approval and export, Retry and the hold) is FINAL-V2
    amendment 1. It is designed and refuted before it is built, and it adds its checks to 9.3 and 9.9:
    - rapid successive edits;
    - failures;
    - reload persistence;
    - actual exports.
